Sure! Here’s a simple yet flavorful way to make an **Indian‑style steak** at home.  
Feel free to adjust spices to your taste.

---

## Ingredients  

| Item | Quantity |
|------|----------|
| Ribeye / sirloin steak (1–1.5 lb) | 1 piece |
| Salt | ½ tsp (to taste) |
| Black pepper | ¼ tsp |
| Garlic cloves | 2–3, minced |
| Fresh ginger | 1 tbsp, grated |
| Red chili powder | 1 tsp (adjust for heat) |
| Garam masala | ½ tsp |
| Turmeric powder | ¼ tsp |
| Ground cumin | ½ tsp |
| Coriander powder | ½ tsp |
| Lemon juice | 1 tbsp |
| Yogurt (plain) | 2 tbsp |
| Butter | 2 tbsp |
| Oil (vegetable or canola) | 1 tbsp |
| Fresh cilantro (optional) | 1 tbsp, chopped |

> **Tip:** If you prefer a milder version, reduce the chili powder or use a sweet paprika instead.

---

## Marinade (Optional but recommended)

1. In a bowl, combine yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, salt, pepper, red chili powder, garam masala, turmeric, cumin, and coriander.  
2. Add the steak, coat it evenly, cover, and refrigerate for **at least 30 min** (up to 4 h).  
   *If you’re short on time, skip the yogurt and just rub the spice mix onto the steak.*

---

## Cooking Steps

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | **Preheat** a cast‑iron skillet or heavy pan over high heat until smoking hot. |
| 2 | **Add oil** (about 1 tsp) and swirl to coat the bottom. |
| 3 | **Sear the steak**: Place the steak in the pan, sear each side for 2–3 min until a golden crust forms. |
| 4 | **Reduce heat** to medium. Add butter (2 tbsp) and let it melt. |
| 5 | **Baste**: Tilt the pan slightly, spoon melted butter over the steak repeatedly for 1–2 min. |
| 6 | **Finish cooking**: Use a meat thermometer – aim for 125°F (52°C) for rare, 135°F (57°C) for medium‑rare, 145°F (63°C) for medium. Adjust time accordingly. |
| 7 | **Rest**: Transfer steak to a cutting board, tent loosely with foil, and rest for 5–10 min. |
| 8 | **Slice & serve**: Slice against the grain, drizzle remaining butter over slices, sprinkle fresh cilantro if desired. |

---

## Serving Suggestions

| Side | Why it works |
|------|--------------|
| **Garlic naan** | Soft bread to soak up juices. |
| **Cucumber raita** | Cooling contrast to spicy steak. |
| **Roasted cauliflower** | Adds texture and mild flavor. |
| **Mint chutney** | Bright, herbal finish. |

---

### Quick FAQ

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Can I use a different cut?** | Yes—sirloin, strip steak, or even a lean flank steak will work. |
| **What about vegetarian options?** | Try paneer tikka or tofu “steak” marinated similarly. |
| **How do I keep the steak juicy?** | Resting is key; also avoid over‑slicing before it rests. |

Enjoy your homemade Indian‑style steak! Let me know how it turns out or if you'd like variations.
